examples.question_text: At an angle of $360^{\circ}$, find the point $P$ on the unit circle and hence evaluate sine, cosine and tangent.
Evaluate (a) $\cos900^{\circ}$ and (b) $\sin(-450^{\circ})$ using the unit circle.
examples.solution_text:
(a) Subtract full revolutions:

$\begin{aligned}900^{\circ}-2(360^{\circ})&=180^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

The terminal point is $(-1,0)$, so $\cos900^{\circ}=-1$.

(b) Add full revolutions:

$\begin{aligned}-450^{\circ}+2(360^{\circ})&=270^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

The terminal point is $(0,-1)$, so $\sin(-450^{\circ})=-1$.

examples.question_text: Evaluate (a) $\tan720^{\circ}$ and (b) $\tan(-270^{\circ})$. Explain any undefined result.
examples.solution_text:
(a) $720^{\circ}-2(360^{\circ})=0^{\circ}$, giving the unit-circle point $(1,0)$.

$\begin{aligned}\tan720^{\circ}&=\frac{0}{1}\\&=0\end{aligned}$

(b) $-270^{\circ}+360^{\circ}=90^{\circ}$, giving the unit-circle point $(0,1)$.

$\tan(-270^{\circ})=\frac{1}{0}$ is undefined because division by zero is undefined.
